title: A Hibernating Bear's Heart Slows to 9 Beats a Minute for Months

scenes.text: A hibernating bear's heart beats nine times a minute.
In summer it beats about 55. Sometimes 20 seconds pass between beats.
For five to seven months, the bear doesn't eat, drink, or go to the toilet.
Its body temperature barely drops. Its metabolism falls to about a quarter.
Researchers at the University of Alaska studied rescued black bears to find out how.
Nine beats a minute, all winter. Then spring.

description:
A hibernating black bear's heart rate drops from about 55 beats a minute to nine.
It goes five to seven months without eating, drinking or going to the toilet, and its metabolism drops to roughly a quarter of normal.
Could you sleep for months? Comment below.
first_comment: The bear's body temperature only drops about ten degrees, yet its metabolism falls to a quarter. Which animal would you want to study next?
